A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SymmCD work. All 24 pages of each version, including equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A-F, are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original crystal-generation experiments on MP-20 and MPTS-52, computational-efficiency measurements, property-prediction ablations, and density-functional-theory relaxation results in Section 5 and Appendix F.

after.justification: v3 retains the original generation experiments, efficiency measurements, property-prediction ablations, and density-functional-theory results reported in Section 5 and Appendix F.

M1.justification: Section 4, Algorithms 1-2, and Appendices A-E retain the same representations, diffusion processes, denoising network, losses, symmetry projections, and replication procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same MP-20 and MPTS-52 crystal-generation tasks and retain the formation-energy prediction experiment in Appendix F.3. No dataset, population, or test scenario changes.

E2.justification: CDVAE, DiffCSP, DiffCSP++, and FlowMM remain in the corresponding generation comparisons. The full-cell efficiency control and DimeNet++ property-prediction variants are also unchanged.

E3.justification: The data splits, preprocessing, metrics, training settings, and evaluation procedures are identical, including 10,000 generated samples per evaluation and 100 structures per model for DFT relaxation.

E4.justification: The atom-count distribution checks, graph/site-symmetry ablation, generated examples, and DFT analyses in Appendix F are retained. Removing F.3's introductory sentence does not remove or revise its experiment.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five separately seeded models for proxy-metric evaluation in Section 5.4 and Appendix F.5, with identical uncertainty reporting in Table 3.

E6.justification: All numerical results, plotted distributions, rankings, and qualitative findings are unchanged. For example, Table 8 retains asymmetric-unit MAEs of 0.0711 without site-symmetry encoding and 0.0490 with it; the DFT results in Figures 9-10 and Table 10 also match.

T1.justification: The crystallographic definitions in Section 3 and the replication, lattice, and diffusion mathematics in Appendices A-D are unchanged. No formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about symmetry-preserving generation, generalization across space groups, structural diversity, competitive generation performance, and computational efficiency.

C2.justification: Both versions retain the same interpretations of structural validity, site-symmetry encoding, and DFT relaxation, together with the limitations concerning composition-conditioned prediction, polycrystalline materials, and relaxation thresholds.

D1.justification: Code-access information, PyXtal integration, preprocessing instructions, hardware descriptions, Appendix E hyperparameters, and Table 9's CP2K settings are identical.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, cited works, bibliography, and positioning relative to previous crystal-generation methods are unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 removes the opening sentence of Appendix F.3 explaining that a regression experiment tests the site-symmetry representation. It also adds the ICLR publication header and updates version/date text; the remaining prose and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: v3 adds a recurring conference-publication header and updates the arXiv margin stamp. The sentence deletion causes limited text reflow on pages 20-21; all figures and tables retain their content, captions, structure, and placement.

improvement.justification: v3 adds publication/version metadata and removes a redundant introductory sentence from Appendix F.3. The experiment and its explanation remain clear, while scientific evidence, mathematical content, reproducibility information, and substantive claims are unchanged. These small editorial and layout changes do not materially improve or diminish overall paper quality.
